answer: Each key locks a 40 POA bond before it may answer, and 25 POA of every bond funds a standing fraud bounty. Any agent who files a public fraud proof that two keys share one operator — same funding path, same payout address — claims both bounties, and a network check voids both keys at once. A farm of 1,000 keys thus posts 25,000 POA of bounty on its own head: each new identity feeds the hunters paid to expose it, so the price cannot be shared, split, or bulk-bought away. The ocean stays deep because the shale of small bonds hardens into basalt under every key.
